message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Compute Engine VM with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
It includes both the `gcloud` CLI command (the easiest way) and the equivalent **REST API** payload you could POST to the Compute Engine endpoint if you prefer to call the API directly.

> ⚠️ **Prerequisites**  
> * You must have a Google Cloud project with billing enabled.  
> * The **Compute Engine API** must be enabled (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`).  
> * You need the **gcloud SDK** installed and authenticated (`gcloud auth login`).  
> * Replace placeholders like `<PROJECT_ID>`, `<ZONE>`, `<INSTANCE_NAME>` with your own values.  

---

## 1️⃣  gcloud CLI Command

```bash
# Variables – replace with your own values
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # e.g., us-central1-a, europe-west4-b, asia-east1-c
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-demo"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
    --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
    --zone="$ZONE" \
    --machine-type="n1-standard-8" \   # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed
    --accelerator="type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1" \
    --image-family="ubuntu-2004-lts" \
    --image-project="ubuntu-os-cloud" \
    --boot-disk-size="100GB" \
    --boot-disk-type="pd-ssd" \
    --maintenance-policy="TERMINATE" \
    --restart-on-failure \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \   # optional: custom init script
    --tags=http-server,https-server \
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration. `n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs & 30 GB RAM. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds one RTX A6000 GPU (`nvidia-tesla-a6000`). |
| `--image-family` + `--image-project` | Boots from the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size` / `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk of 100 GB. |
| `--maintenance-policy` | Terminates the VM during host maintenance (default). |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Auto‑restarts if the VM crashes. |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional shell script that runs at first boot. |
| `--tags` | Enables HTTP/HTTPS firewall rules. |
| `--scopes` | Grants full Cloud Platform access (adjust scopes if you need tighter security). |

---

## 2️⃣  REST API Call (JSON)

If you want to call the Compute Engine API directly (e.g., from a custom application), you can POST the following JSON to:

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/<ZONE>/instances
```

```json
{
  "name": "<INSTANCE_NAME>",
  "machineType": "projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/<ZONE>/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/<ZONE>/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/<ZONE>/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  },
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-470"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

> **Authentication** – Use OAuth 2.0 Bearer token (`Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>`) obtained via the Google Cloud SDK or your preferred authentication flow.

---

## 3️⃣  Quick Checklist

1. **Enable GPU quota** – Make sure your project has GPU quota for the `nvidia-tesla-a6000` accelerator in the chosen zone.  
2. **Firewall rules** – The `--tags` flag automatically creates firewall rules for HTTP/HTTPS. If you need other ports, add them manually.  
3. **GPU drivers** – The optional `startup-script` installs NVIDIA driver 470. Adjust the driver version if newer releases are required.  
4. **Billing** – GPU instances incur higher costs. Verify your budget before launching.  

---

### Example Output

After running the `gcloud` command, you’ll see something like:

```
Created [https://www.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/instances/rtx-a6000-demo].
```

You can then SSH into the instance:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-demo --project=my-gcp-project --zone=us-central1-a
```

Once logged in, verify the GPU:

```bash
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version.

Happy computing! 🚀
